title: How Long Does Cooked Chicken Last in the Fridge?

seo.title: How Long Cooked Chicken Lasts in the Fridge
seo.meta_description: Cooked chicken generally keeps 3–4 days in a refrigerator at 40°F/4°C or below. Learn how to cool, store, reheat and know when to discard it.
seo.search_intent: Safe refrigerator storage of cooked chicken.

excerpt: USDA recommends using refrigerated cooked chicken within 3–4 days when it has been cooled promptly and kept at 40°F/4°C or below.
content_html:
Cooked chicken generally keeps for 3–4 days in the refrigerator, according to USDA guidance, provided it was cooled promptly and the refrigerator stays at 40°F / 4°C or below.

The clock is only part of the answer. Chicken that sat out for hours before refrigeration may be unsafe even if it has been in the fridge for only one day.

Quick storage guide

SituationGuidance
Cooked chicken, properly refrigerated3–4 days
Left at room temperatureRefrigerate within 2 hours
Outdoor temperature above 90°F / 32°CRefrigerate within 1 hour
Not going to eat it in timeFreeze promptly

Why cooling matters

Refrigeration slows bacterial growth; it does not sterilize food. A deep container of hot chicken can cool slowly in the center, so dividing large amounts into shallow containers helps the food move through warm temperatures more quickly.

You do not need to leave cooked chicken on the counter until it becomes completely cold. Prompt refrigeration in smaller portions is safer than letting a large dish sit out for hours.

The two-hour rule

Perishable food should generally be refrigerated within 2 hours. When the surrounding temperature is above 90°F / 32°C, such as at a picnic or summer cookout, the limit drops to 1 hour.

Putting chicken in the refrigerator after it has already spent too long warm does not reset the risk.

How to store leftovers

Use clean, covered containers and keep cooked chicken above raw meat or poultry to prevent drips. A refrigerator thermometer is useful because the dial setting does not always reflect the actual temperature.

If you cooked a whole chicken, portioning it before storage can help it cool faster and avoids repeatedly warming and handling the entire bird.

Can you eat refrigerated chicken cold?

Yes. Properly cooked, cooled and refrigerated chicken can be eaten cold within the 3–4 day window. Reheating is not required simply because it was refrigerated.

How to reheat it

USDA recommends reheating leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Microwaves can create hot and cold spots, so rotate pieces, stir shredded chicken and allow a short standing time after heating.

Reheating cannot make poorly stored chicken safe again. Heat is not a substitute for proper cooling and storage.

Do smell and appearance tell you enough?

Off odors, sliminess and obvious spoilage are reasons to discard chicken. But disease-causing bacteria do not always produce a smell or visible change. A normal smell does not extend the 3–4 day storage recommendation.

When freezing makes sense

If you know you will not eat the chicken within a few days, freeze it early rather than waiting until day four. Package it in meal-sized portions and label the date.

Freezing stops microbial growth while food remains frozen, but it does not rescue food that was already left out too long or showing spoilage.

Discard it sooner when

  • it sat out longer than 2 hours, or longer than 1 hour above 90°F;
  • the refrigerator lost power or stayed above 40°F for an extended period;
  • it has an off odor, slimy surface or obvious mold;
  • raw poultry juices may have contaminated it;
  • you cannot determine when it was cooked.

Bottom line

Keep cooked chicken at 40°F / 4°C or below and use it within 3–4 days. Refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when temperatures are above 90°F. Freeze early if you will not finish it in time.

Sources

Storage times and temperatures come from FoodSafety.gov and USDA FSIS.

faq.question: Can I eat cooked chicken after 5 days?
faq.answer: USDA recommends 3–4 days in the refrigerator. After day 4, smell alone is not a reliable reason to keep it.

faq.question: Should chicken cool completely before refrigeration?
faq.answer: No. Divide large amounts into shallow containers and refrigerate promptly rather than leaving them out for hours.
